events.content: Marvell Technology data center revenue Q2 fiscal year 2027 custom AI silicon optics

**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2027 AI/Data-Center read-through:** Marvell reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$2.739 billion** for the quarter ended **August 1, 2026**, up **37% year over year** and **13% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.33** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.94**. [[1]]

**Data center was the central driver:** Data-center revenue reached **$2.172 billion**, up **46% YoY** and **18% QoQ**, and represented **79%** of company revenue, versus 74% a year earlier. [[2]] This implies that virtually all of Marvell’s near-term growth thesis is now linked to hyperscale AI infrastructure rather than its communications-and-other businesses. [[2]]

**Guidance moved materially higher:** Management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to **$3.15 billion ±5%**, which at the midpoint implies roughly **15% sequential growth** and more than **50% YoY growth**; it also raised FY2027 revenue expectations to approximately **$12 billion** and FY2028 expectations to approximately **$18 billion**. [[2]] [[3]] Management expects data-center revenue to grow about **60% in FY2027** and more than **60% in FY2028**. [[4]] [[3]]

**Custom AI silicon is shifting from design-win narrative to revenue ramp:** Marvell said its Custom business should accelerate significantly in the second half of FY2027, with growth coming from both **XPU** programs and **XPU-attach** products, including custom NICs and CXL-related products. [[1]] [[4]] The disclosed expanded hyperscaler warrant agreement covers existing custom programs, new design wins, and potential future programs spanning AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory-interface controllers, and near-memory compute. [[4]] The important investment implication is that custom silicon can add a second major AI engine alongside connectivity, but it may also pressure gross margin as its revenue mix rises. [[4]] [[3]]

**Electro-optics/connectivity remains the nearer-term revenue base:** Marvell cited strong demand across connectivity, including **800G and 1.6T scale-out optics**, **51.2T Ethernet switches**, scale-up optical solutions for **NPO/CPO**, and coherent **1.6T ZR/ZR+** modules for data-center interconnect. [[5]] [[6]] Management said 800G demand remains strong, 1.6T is ramping rapidly, and 51.2T products are expected to drive more than a doubling of scale-out-switching revenue during FY2027. [[6]]

events.content: Marvell Q2 FY2027 custom AI silicon revenue figure electro-optics revenue breakdown

**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended August 2, 2025):** total revenue reached a record **$2.006 billion**, up **58% year over year** and **6% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.22** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.67**. [[1]]

**Data center was the core growth engine:** revenue was **$1.491 billion**, representing **74% of company revenue**, up **69% year over year** and **3% sequentially** from $1.441 billion in Q1 FY2026. [[2]]

**Custom AI silicon and electro-optics:** management identified strong AI demand for these two product categories as a principal driver of the quarter’s growth, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with **more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers**. [[2, 3]] 

Marvell did **not** disclose separate Q2 revenue amounts for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics; rather, it stated on the earnings call that the two product lines together accounted for **more than three quarters of data-center revenue**, implying more than roughly **$1.1 billion** of the $1.491 billion data-center total. [[4, 2]] 

For Q3 FY2026, Marvell guided total revenue to **$2.060 billion ±5%**; management expected overall data-center revenue to be approximately flat sequentially, as electro-optics strength offsets a near-term decline in custom revenue, while expecting custom-business growth to become substantially stronger in Q4. [[2, 4]]

**Bottom line:** Q2 demonstrated that Marvell’s AI exposure is already highly material—data center supplied nearly three quarters of revenue and its custom/optical franchises comprised the majority of that segment—but the Q3 outlook also illustrates that custom-silicon ramps can be nonlinear and customer-program timing can create quarterly volatility. [[2, 4]]

events.content: Marvell FY2027 full year data center revenue guidance custom silicon optics

Marvell’s FY2026 ended January 31, 2026, and generated $8.195 billion of total revenue; management said data-center revenue “surpassed $6 billion,” up 46% year over year. [[1]] [[2]]

| FY2026 data-center revenue split | Revenue / share |
|---|---:|
| Optical interconnect / optics | **Roughly half of data-center revenue**, implying **just over ~$3.0 billion** |
| Custom silicon | **~$1.5 billion**, or **approximately 25%** of data-center revenue |
| Other data-center products—e.g., switching, storage, and remaining interconnect | **Roughly 25%**, implying **about ~$1.5 billion-plus** |

Marvell’s own proxy describes optical interconnect as “roughly half” of FY2026 data-center revenue and custom silicon as “approximately 25%”; therefore, these are management-reported mix percentages rather than a formally disclosed, exact audited product-revenue table. [[3]] 

The custom-silicon figure is the clearest absolute disclosure: management said custom revenue doubled year over year to **$1.5 billion** in FY2026. [[2]] 

Accordingly, the practical FY2026 **custom silicon vs. optics split** is approximately **$1.5 billion custom / >$3.0 billion optics**, or about **25% / 50%** of the data-center business, respectively. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Marvell automotive Ethernet business sale fiscal year 2025 2026

events.content: Marvell automotive Ethernet business sale fiscal year 2025 2026

Marvell agreed on April 7, 2025 to sell its Automotive Ethernet business—including the Brightlane® Automotive Ethernet portfolio and related assets—to Infineon Technologies for **$2.5 billion in cash**; Marvell’s board approved the transaction. [[1]] 

The transaction closed on **August 14, 2025**, after receiving required regulatory approvals. [[2]] [[3]] 

The disposed business was expected to generate **$225 million–$250 million of FY2026 revenue**, implying an enterprise-value-to-forward-revenue valuation of roughly **10.0x–11.1x**. [[1]] [[2]] 

For Marvell, the sale further concentrates the company on data infrastructure: data center had represented **75% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 fourth quarter**, according to CEO Matt Murphy. [[1]] 

Marvell recorded a **$1.8 billion pre-tax gain on sale** in FY2026 third quarter, and stated that the divestiture was not expected to have a material effect on non-GAAP EPS. [[4]] [[2]] 

For Infineon, the acquisition expands its automotive semiconductor and software-defined-vehicle capabilities; it placed the acquired operation into a new **“Ethernet Solutions”** business line in its Automotive division. [[3]] 

Infineon said the acquired business had approximately **$4 billion of design-win pipeline through 2030**, expected calendar-2025 revenue of **$225 million–$250 million**, and a gross margin of about **60%**; it funded the acquisition with existing liquidity plus additional debt capital. [[3]]

For Q3 FY2027, Marvell guided total company revenue to roughly **$3.15 billion** (±5%), while an industry analysis estimated data-center revenue would rise about **20% sequentially** and **75% year over year**; applying 20% to Q2’s $2.172 billion implies approximately **$2.61 billion** in Q3 data-center revenue. [[2]] [[1]] 

The expected Q3 step-up reflects broad data-center demand, with management specifically citing strong connectivity demand and a **significant acceleration in Custom silicon beginning in the second half of FY2027**. [[1]] 

Marvell does **not** disclose quarterly revenue separately for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics in its reported end-market table; however, its FY2026 investor materials characterize optical interconnect as roughly **half of data-center revenue** and custom silicon as approximately **25%** of data-center revenue. [[3]] 

A third-party model estimated Q2 FY2027 electro-optical-component revenue at approximately **$1.4 billion**, up **97.2% year over year**, indicating that optics remained the larger near-term AI revenue contributor even as custom silicon began to accelerate. [[2]] 

The relevant product set includes 800G and 1.6T scale-out optics, NPO/CPO scale-up optical solutions, data-center interconnect modules, and custom XPU/XPU-attach solutions. [[4]]
